source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: Public 14:1 binds Hebrew 13:23; public 14:2–15 binds Hebrew 14:1–14. All other selected verses bind matching labels.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Makes the people’s action explicit and retains the father–son succession.
verses.before: The people of the land took Jehoahaz son of Josiah and made him king in place of his father in Jerusalem.
verses.after: The people of the land took Josiah’s son Jehoahaz and made him king in Jerusalem in his father’s place.
verses.tsw_comparator: The people of the land took Jehoahaz son of Josiah and made him king in place of his father in Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Preserves both the accession age and the exceptionally short reign.
verses.before: Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem.
verses.after: Jehoahaz was twenty-three when he became king. He reigned in Jerusalem for three months.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Retains the location and unequal silver and gold amounts; explains the imposed payment through levy.
verses.before: The king of Egypt removed him at Jerusalem and imposed upon the land a fine of one hundred talents of silver and one talent of gold.
verses.after: The king of Egypt removed him from power in Jerusalem and imposed a levy on the land of one hundred talents of silver and one talent of gold.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king of Egypt removed him at Jerusalem and imposed upon the land a fine of one hundred talents of silver and one talent of gold.

verses.rationale: Repeats Jehoahaz to make the brothers and the Egyptian king’s actions clear.
verses.before: The king of Egypt made Eliakim his brother king over Judah and Jerusalem and changed his name to Jehoiakim. Neco took Jehoahaz his brother and brought him to Egypt.
verses.after: The king of Egypt made Jehoahaz’s brother Eliakim king over Judah and Jerusalem and changed his name to Jehoiakim. Neco took Eliakim’s brother Jehoahaz away to Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king of Egypt made Eliakim his brother king over Judah and Jerusalem and changed his name to Jehoiakim. Neco took Jehoahaz his brother and brought him to Egypt.

verses.rationale: Keeps the evaluation tied to his God and preserves age and duration.
verses.before: Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD his God.
verses.after: Jehoiakim was twenty-five when he became king. He reigned in Jerusalem for eleven years and did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD his God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD his God.

verses.rationale: Preserves the purpose clause without asserting here that the proposed deportation happened.
verses.before: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against him and bound him with bronze chains to take him to Babylon.
verses.after: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came against him and bound him in bronze shackles to take him to Babylon.
verses.tsw_comparator: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against him and bound him with bronze chains to take him to Babylon.

verses.rationale: Keeps the partial removal and palace/temple ambiguity in a note on hekal.
verses.before: Nebuchadnezzar also brought some of the vessels of the house of the LORD to Babylon and put them in his palace in Babylon.
verses.after: Nebuchadnezzar also took some of the vessels from the LORD’s house to Babylon and put them in his palace there.
verses.tsw_comparator: Nebuchadnezzar also brought some of the vessels of the house of the LORD to Babylon and put them in his palace in Babylon.

verses.rationale: Retains both the deeds and the less specific findings against him without inventing charges.
verses.before: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoiakim, the detestable things that he did and what was found against him, look, they are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah. Jehoiachin his son became king in his place.
verses.after: The rest of Jehoiakim’s acts, the detestable things he did, and what was found against him are recorded in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah. His son Jehoiachin succeeded him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoiakim, the detestable things that he did and what was found against him, look, they are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah. Jehoiachin his son became king in his place.

verses.rationale: Retains the pinned Hebrew age eight and the precise duration; notes the difference from Kings rather than harmonizing.
verses.before: Jehoiachin was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned three months and ten days in Jerusalem. He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD.
verses.after: Jehoiachin was eight when he became king. He reigned in Jerusalem for three months and ten days and did what was evil in the LORD’s eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoiachin was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned three months and ten days in Jerusalem. He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains the Hebrew brother relationship in the text and explains the uncle relationship in Kings separately.
verses.before: At the turning of the year King Nebuchadnezzar sent and brought him to Babylon, with the precious vessels of the house of the LORD, and made Zedekiah his brother king over Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.after: At the turn of the year, King Nebuchadnezzar sent for him and brought him to Babylon, along with the precious vessels from the LORD’s house. He made Jehoiachin’s brother Zedekiah king over Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the turning of the year King Nebuchadnezzar sent and brought him to Babylon, with the precious vessels of the house of the LORD, and made Zedekiah his brother king over Judah and Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Keeps the age and reign length in the recurring readable accession formula.
verses.before: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem.
verses.after: Zedekiah was twenty-one when he became king. He reigned in Jerusalem for eleven years.
verses.tsw_comparator: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Unfolds from the mouth of the LORD without obscuring the source of Jeremiah’s message.
verses.before: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD his God. He did not humble himself before Jeremiah the prophet, who spoke from the mouth of the LORD.
verses.after: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD his God. He did not humble himself before the prophet Jeremiah, who spoke the LORD’s words.
verses.tsw_comparator: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD his God. He did not humble himself before Jeremiah the prophet, who spoke from the mouth of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves the oath and both bodily images, with returning connected to the book’s recurring language.
verses.before: He also rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear by God. He stiffened his neck and hardened his heart from turning to the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.after: He also rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear an oath by God. He stiffened his neck and hardened his heart against returning to the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: He also rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear by God. He stiffened his neck and hardened his heart from turning to the LORD, the God of Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains cumulative unfaithfulness and the contrast between consecration and defilement without adding an ethnic judgment.
verses.before: Moreover, all the officials of the priests and the people acted very unfaithfully according to all the detestable practices of the nations, and they polluted the house of the LORD that he had consecrated in Jerusalem.
verses.after: All the leading priests and the people kept adding to their unfaithfulness, following all the detestable practices of the nations. They defiled the LORD’s house, which he had made holy in Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moreover, all the officials of the priests and the people acted very unfaithfully according to all the detestable practices of the nations, and they polluted the house of the LORD that he had consecrated in Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Renders the repeated early sending idiom as persistent action and keeps compassion as the stated reason.
verses.before: The LORD, the God of their ancestors, sent word to them by the hand of his messengers, rising early and sending, because he had compassion on his people and on his dwelling place.
verses.after: The LORD, the God of their ancestors, kept sending word to them through his messengers, again and again. He had compassion on his people and on his dwelling place.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD, the God of their ancestors, sent word to them by the hand of his messengers, rising early and sending, because he had compassion on his people and on his dwelling place.

verses.rationale: Preserves the three escalating actions and the final healing metaphor rather than smoothing the judgment.
verses.before: But they mocked the messengers of God, despised his words, and scoffed at his prophets until the wrath of the LORD rose against his people, until there was no remedy.
verses.after: But they mocked God’s messengers, despised his words, and scoffed at his prophets, until the LORD’s wrath rose against his people and there was no remedy.
verses.tsw_comparator: But they mocked the messengers of God, despised his words, and scoffed at his prophets until the wrath of the LORD rose against his people, until there was no remedy.

verses.rationale: Keeps the sanctuary killing and differentiated victims explicit; makes the agents readable without softening the violence.
verses.before: So he brought up against them the king of the Chaldeans, who killed their young men with the sword in the house of their sanctuary and had no compassion on young man or virgin, old man or aged. He gave them all into his hand.
verses.after: He brought the king of the Chaldeans against them. The king killed their young men with the sword in their sanctuary and showed no compassion to young man or virgin, to the old or the very aged. God handed them all over to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: So he brought up against them the king of the Chaldeans, who killed their young men with the sword in the house of their sanctuary and had no compassion on young man or virgin, old man or aged. He gave them all into his hand.

verses.rationale: Retains the exhaustive list and both divine designations in the source.
verses.before: All the vessels of the house of God, great and small, the treasures of the house of the LORD, and the treasures of the king and his officials, all these he brought to Babylon.
verses.after: He took everything to Babylon: all the vessels of God’s house, large and small, the treasures of the LORD’s house, and the treasures of the king and his officials.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the vessels of the house of God, great and small, the treasures of the house of the LORD, and the treasures of the king and his officials, all these he brought to Babylon.

verses.rationale: Preserves each destructive action and the distinction between sacred and royal buildings.
verses.before: They burned the house of God, tore down the wall of Jerusalem, burned all its palaces with fire, and destroyed all its precious vessels.
verses.after: They burned down God’s house, tore down Jerusalem’s wall, burned all its palaces, and destroyed everything precious in them.
verses.tsw_comparator: They burned the house of God, tore down the wall of Jerusalem, burned all its palaces with fire, and destroyed all its precious vessels.

verses.rationale: Makes the captives’ subjection explicit while keeping its stated endpoint.
verses.before: People who escaped from the sword he carried to Babylon, and they became servants to him and his sons until the rule of the kingdom of Persia,
verses.after: He carried off to Babylon those who had escaped the sword. They became slaves to him and his sons until the kingdom of Persia came to power.
verses.tsw_comparator: Those who escaped from the sword he carried to Babylon, and they became servants to him and his sons until the rule of the kingdom of Persia,

verses.rationale: Retains the land’s Sabbath image and seventy years without importing a harmonized chronology.
verses.before: to fulfill the word of the LORD by the mouth of Jeremiah until the land had enjoyed its Sabbaths. All the days of its desolation it kept Sabbath, to fulfill seventy years.
verses.after: This fulfilled the LORD’s word spoken through Jeremiah. The land made up for its Sabbaths: throughout its desolation it rested, until seventy years were complete.
verses.tsw_comparator: to fulfill the word of the LORD by the mouth of Jeremiah until the land had enjoyed its Sabbaths. All the days of its desolation it kept Sabbath, to fulfill seventy years.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine initiative, fulfillment, and the proclamation’s spoken and written forms.
verses.before: In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, so that the word of the LORD by the mouth of Jeremiah might be fulfilled, the LORD stirred the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, and he made a proclamation throughout all his kingdom and also put it in writing, saying,
verses.after: In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, the LORD stirred Cyrus’s spirit to fulfill the word the LORD had spoken through Jeremiah. Cyrus issued a proclamation throughout his kingdom and also put it in writing:
verses.tsw_comparator: In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, so that the word of the LORD by the mouth of Jeremiah might be fulfilled, the LORD stirred the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, and he made a proclamation throughout all his kingdom and also put it in writing, saying,

verses.rationale: Retains Cyrus’s sweeping royal claim and ends with the source’s invitation to go up, leaving the return ahead.
verses.before: “Thus says Cyrus king of Persia: The LORD, the God of the heavens, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and he has appointed me to build for him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. Whoever is among you from all his people— may the LORD his God be with him. Let him go up!”
verses.after: “This is what Cyrus king of Persia says: ‘The LORD, the God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth. He has appointed me to build him a house in Jerusalem, in Judah. Whoever among you belongs to his people—may the LORD his God be with him, and let him go up!’”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Thus says Cyrus king of Persia: The LORD, the God of the heavens, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and he has appointed me to build for him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. Whoever is among you from all his people— may the LORD his God be with him. Let him go up!”

comparative_references.scope: All 23 TSW verses read after drafting independently from every pinned source verse and its source notes.
